10.2.s: śarkvarīṣu ṣoḍaśinā stuvīteti gaurīvitaṃ mahānāmnīṣu syādṛkcodanā hi tatprakaraṇe
10.2.d: शर्क्वरीषु षोडशिना स्तुवीतेति गौरीवितं महानाम्नीषु स्यादृक्चोदना हि तत्प्रकरणे
10.2.m: To the rule, "one should praise with the ṣoḍaśin on the Śarkvarī verses," the Gaurīvita should be on the Mahānāmnī verses, because of the injunction of verses in that context.
Rather, the Mahānāmnī verses themselves should be the ṣoḍaśin-sāman, for no other sāman is assigned to them.

10.2.s: api ha pṛṣṭhastotrīyeṣu parokṣāṇi kurvannaitāsu nityavatsāḥ karoti
10.2.d: अपि ह पृष्ठस्तोत्रीयेषु परोक्षाणि कुर्वन्नैतासु नित्यवत्साः करोति
10.2.m: Moreover, even when making invisible substitutes in the pṛṣṭha strophic verses, one does not do so in these [Mahānāmnī verses], like the regular calf.
And they are prescribed in this place for the Vajra.

10.2.s: virāṭsvanuṣṭupsu ca gaurīvitameva syātsvāraprāyāṇi hi ṣoḍaśisāmāni
10.2.d: विराट्स्वनुष्टुप्सु च गौरीवितमेव स्यात्स्वारप्रायाणि हि षोडशिसामानि
10.2.m: And in the virāj and anuṣṭubh verses, there should be the Gaurīvita alone, for ṣoḍaśin-sāmans are mostly of the svāra type.
The optional cadences of the Śarkvarī verses should be in the places of the iḍā, say the teachers, for that is the majority.
Only in the udders [of the verses], say Gautama and Dhānañjayya, for here [the text] mentions the cadence-statement.
In place of the word 'atha', says Śaucivṛkṣi, for thus the modification is smaller.
Because there is no restriction, in all cadence places, says Kautsa.
The purīṣa verses are connected with the last strophic verse, because of immediately succeeding it, says Dhānañjayya.
[The text] says: "having praised with the Śarkvarī verses," concluding [them], "with the purīṣa"; therefore it should be unconnected.
It should be at the end of a round, or at the end of a stotra.

10.2.s: pañcame'hani rāyovājīyaṃ brahmasāma kurvstasya sthāne kuryāt yat kalpavṛttenopapannam
10.2.d: पञ्चमेऽहनि रायोवाजीयं ब्रह्मसाम कुर्व्स्तस्य स्थाने कुर्यात् यत् कल्पवृत्तेनोपपन्नम्
10.2.m: On the fifth day, when performing the Rāyovājīya as the brahman's sāman, in its place one should perform that which is suitable according to the rule of ritual practice.

10.2.s: bārhadgiraṃ kuryādaraṇye geyhi sacchandasyañca samāne cāhani dṛṣṭam
10.2.d: बार्हद्गिरं कुर्यादरण्ये गेय्हि सच्छन्दस्यञ्च समाने चाहनि दृष्टम्
10.2.m: One should perform the Bārhadgira, which is forest-sung, in the same metre, and seen on the same day.
When performing the Pārthuraśma, one should perform it on the verses of the Bārhadgira, so that there is no shifting of verses.

10.3.m: Some say that the Mānasa stotra is not a subordinate part of the tenth day, because it occurs outside the wife's offerings and because it has no place for a stotra.
And [the text] speaks of its creation as a separate limb.
However, it must be a subordinate part, because it is handed down in the sacred text under the governing rule [of that day].
As for the statement that "it has no place for a stotra," even for a single stotra there is no independent existence [apart from the rite].

10.3.s: agniṣṭomāvabhita iti vādamātraṃ yathā yadukthyo yajñakratoranantarayāyetyatirātrasya gavāmayane
10.3.d: अग्निष्टोमावभित इति वादमात्रं यथा यदुक्थ्यो यज्ञक्रतोरनन्तरयायेत्यतिरात्रस्य गवामयने
10.3.m: The phrase "on both sides are agniṣṭoma sacrifices" is a mere laudatory statement, just as in the Gavāmayana: "that which is an ukthya should immediately follow the sacrificial rite [of the atirātra]."
Nor does that which is taught under the governing rule become a non-part merely because of being a limb of creation, just as the Rathantara [is a part] of the Jyotiṣṭoma.

10.3.s: atirātrayoḥ ṣoḍaśinyanādiṣṭe pratiṣiddhe vā kriyamāṇe yatra virāḍupapadyeta kuryyādenaṃ tatretyācāryyā dvādaśāhe hi kriyate na gavāmayane tatra tathopapadyate
10.3.d: अतिरात्रयोः षोडशिन्यनादिष्टे प्रतिषिद्धे वा क्रियमाणे यत्र विराडुपपद्येत कुर्य्यादेनं तत्रेत्याचार्य्या द्वादशाहे हि क्रियते न गवामयने तत्र तथोपपद्यते
10.3.m: When the ṣoḍaśin is not enjoined or is prohibited in the two atirātra sacrifices, but is being performed, one should perform it wherever the virāj metre is suitable, say the teachers; for it is performed in the twelve-day rite, but not in the Gavāmayana; there it is suitable in that way.

10.3.s: akāraṇantu sampadbahavo hyavirāṭsampannāḥ kāraṇañcāpūrvasya vidherna vidyate
10.3.d: अकारणन्तु सम्पद्बहवो ह्यविराट्सम्पन्नाः कारणञ्चापूर्वस्य विधेर्न विद्यते
10.3.m: However, numerical conformity is not a cause, for many [rites] are accomplished without virāj conformity, and there is no cause for a novel injunction.

10.3.s: yāthākāmī tvatirātrasya prakṛtau tasmādihāpi tathaiva syāt
10.3.d: याथाकामी त्वतिरात्रस्य प्रकृतौ तस्मादिहापि तथैव स्यात्
10.3.m: Moreover, [the ṣoḍaśin] is optional in the basic form of the atirātra sacrifice; therefore here also it should be just the same.
The injunction and prohibition, however, are for the purpose of restriction.
In the former thirteen-day sacrifice, the chandoma days are shifted, because the Somasāman is enjoined and the Gaurīvita is not enjoined.
For according to the principle of the Gavāmayana, the interrupted pṛṣṭhya six-day period proceeds in that way,
because there is no distinction from the ten-day period,
And the first bahiṣpavamāna chant has [the verse beginning with] "pratna", for [the text] says later concerning this: "the corresponding verse of this fall".
And it is seen for the purpose of the tenth day when there is no interruption,
Because of the reference to the year, in the night-sessions the repetition of the abhiplava six-day periods occurs in the very same way, says Gautama.
Others say: [the text] indicates the cessation of the subsequent ones in the thirty-three-day sacrifice.

10.4.s: āvṛttānāṃ pañcāhānāṃ prathamasya pañcāhasya prathamasyāhno mānavādirbṛhatī tajjāmi syātsantaninā
10.4.d: आवृत्तानां पञ्चाहानां प्रथमस्य पञ्चाहस्य प्रथमस्याह्नो मानवादिर्बृहती तज्जामि स्यात्सन्तनिना
10.4.m: Of the repeated five-day periods, on the first day of the first five-day period the bṛhatī begins with the Mānavā verse; that would be monotonous with the Santani.
However, there is cessation [of monotony] because it is a modification.
In five-day periods, one should not introduce the abhiplava.

10.4.s: tān pṛṣṭhyastomapañcāhāneke'nādeśe prakṛtipratyayādviśvajidanvavāyānnānā brahmasāmatvātpṛṣṭhyataḥ ṣaṣṭhasyālopavacanāt jyotirgaurāyurityanādeśāt trivṛtā prayanti trivṛtodyantīti cāha
10.4.d: तान् पृष्ठ्यस्तोमपञ्चाहानेकेऽनादेशे प्रकृतिप्रत्ययाद्विश्वजिदन्ववायान्नाना ब्रह्मसामत्वात्पृष्ठ्यतः षष्ठस्यालोपवचनात् ज्योतिर्गौरायुरित्यनादेशात् त्रिवृता प्रयन्ति त्रिवृतोद्यन्तीति चाह
10.4.m: Some say that when not specified, those [five-day periods] are pṛṣṭhya-stoma five-day periods, because of the rule of the archetype, because of the insertion of the Viśvajit, because of the variety of the brahman's sāmans, because of the statement not to omit the sixth [day] from the pṛṣṭhya, because there is no instruction as "Jyotis, Go, Āyus", and because [the text] says: "They advance with the Trivṛt, they rise with the Trivṛt."

10.4.s: abhiplavapañcāhā eveti gautamo'dhikṛto hi sa satreṣu bhavatītaraścādṛṣṭaḥ
10.4.d: अभिप्लवपञ्चाहा एवेति गौतमोऽधिकृतो हि स सत्रेषु भवतीतरश्चादृष्टः
10.4.m: "They are only abhiplava five-day periods," says Gautama, "for that [abhiplava] is governed in the sattras, whereas the other is unseen.
And from where would there be repetition of this archetypal five-day period?

10.4.s: jyotirgaurāyurgaurāyuḥ pañcāhaḥ sa dvitīyaḥ sa tṛtīya iti ca parabrāhmaṇam
10.4.d: ज्योतिर्गौरायुर्गौरायुः पञ्चाहः स द्वितीयः स तृतीय इति च परब्राह्मणम्
10.4.m: Moreover, another Brāhmaṇa says: 'Jyotiḥ, Gauḥ, Āyuḥ, Gauḥ, Āyuḥ is the five-day period; that is the second, that is the third.'"

10.4.s: eṣa pratnāvārkajambhaṃ vā pratipañcāhaṃ yathā lokabṛhadrathantarāścet
10.4.d: एष प्रत्नावार्कजम्भं वा प्रतिपञ्चाहं यथा लोकबृहद्रथन्तराश्चेत्
10.4.m: This is [chanted on] the Pratnavat, the Ārka, or the Jambha for each five-day period, as [in the case of] the loka, if the Bṛhat and Rathantara [melodies are used].

10.4.s: āñjanābhyañjanāsu gārhapatya upasatsu sarpīṣi phāṇeyuḥ pṛthagdevasurabhibhiryānyuktāni brāhmaṇena
10.4.d: आञ्जनाभ्यञ्जनासु गार्हपत्य उपसत्सु सर्पीषि फाणेयुः पृथग्देवसुरभिभिर्यान्युक्तानि ब्राह्मणेन
10.4.m: At the upasads [connected with] the anointments and unguents, they should clarify ghee separately over the gārhapatya fire along with divine fragrances that are stated in the Brāhmaṇa.

10.4.s: taiḥ sutyāsūpākaraṇavelāyāsavanānāṃ pūrveṇa havirddhāne āsīnāṃ āñjīrannabhyañjīrśca
10.4.d: तैः सुत्यासूपाकरणवेलायासवनानां पूर्वेण हविर्द्धाने आसीनां आञ्जीरन्नभ्यञ्जीर्श्च
10.4.m: With these, at the time of the preliminary rite of the soma-pressing sessions on the soma-pressing days, seated in front of the two soma-carts, they should anoint [their eyes] and rub [their bodies] with unguent.
"Only in the āgnīdhra shed after having eaten," says Gautama.
The sequence has been stated by the Brāhmaṇa.
"Only at the sarvastoma sacrifice," says Gautama.

10.5.s: saṃvatsarasammitāsu prathamaṃ dāśarātrikaṃ prāyaṇīy syādityeke trivṛdeva kāryyamiti hyāheti
10.5.d: संवत्सरसम्मितासु प्रथमं दाशरात्रिकं प्रायणीय् स्यादित्येके त्रिवृदेव कार्य्यमिति ह्याहेति
10.5.m: In [sattras] measured by a year, the initial day should be the first day of the ten-day period, according to some, for [the Brāhmaṇa] says: "The trivṛt [stoma] alone should be performed."
Having prescribed the initial day, however, [the text] introduces the stoma modification for it.
And a performance of a single component of the ten-day [period] is not found.
"When the abhiplava [period] is repeated, the Śākvara-form should be used, in order to maintain the material belonging to the yearly rite," say the teachers.
The fourth abhiplava, however, has been omitted; along with it [the Śākvara-form] would depart, just as the Janitra [sāman departs] along with the pṛṣṭhya [period].
The Santani [sāman] was employed previously, because of its fitness for repetition.

10.5.s: yaṇvantu syādupariṣṭādhyabhiplavānāṃ loṣasthānaṃ pūrvasmin pakṣasi tatpurastādāvṛttānām
10.5.d: यण्वन्तु स्यादुपरिष्टाध्यभिप्लवानां लोषस्थानं पूर्वस्मिन् पक्षसि तत्पुरस्तादावृत्तानाम्
10.5.m: The Yaṇva [sāman], however, should be [employed]; for after the abhiplavas, the clod-place is in the first wing; it is in front of the repeated [abhiplavas].
By this, [the procedure] for the sixty-one-night sacrifice has been explained.

10.5.s: śatarātre'bhiprayāyamabhiṣuṇvantvabhikrāntyai samānatrābhiṣuṇvanti pratiṣṭhityā iti sa vikalpaḥ syāt
10.5.d: शतरात्रेऽभिप्रयायमभिषुण्वन्त्वभिक्रान्त्यै समानत्राभिषुण्वन्ति प्रतिष्ठित्या इति स विकल्पः स्यात्
10.5.m: At the hundred-night sacrifice: "Marching forward, let them press [soma] for advancement; they press [soma] in the same place for stability"—that would be an option.
Advancing, they should press [soma], as in the Sārasvata [sattras];
or in the same place, not advancing at all, as in the other [sattras].

"Having caused the sadas and the cart-sheds to have wheels, they should turn the wheels around when the days conclude," say the teachers; "from that [turning] there is the form of marching forward, and from not moving away there is pressing in the same place."
The time of consecration for the Gavāmayana has been stated by the Brāhmaṇa.
Vaiśākha and Jyaiṣṭha, however, are options alongside the Caitrī fortnight, and also Āṣāḍha.

10.5.s: ṣaṣṭhyāṃ vā dīkṣitvā saptadaśa dīkṣāḥ kurvīran
10.5.d: षष्ठ्यां वा दीक्षित्वा सप्तदश दीक्षाः कुर्वीरन्
10.5.m: Or, having undergone consecration on the sixth day [of the half-month], they should perform seventeen consecrations.
By this has been stated [the rule] for the yearly and non-yearly rites when no specific instruction is given.

10.6.s: pañcasu māḥsu bārhatāḥ pragāthā āpyanta ityabhīvarttastotrīyā brahmasāmabhūtasya tasya hi prakaraṇe śrūyante
10.6.d: पञ्चसु माःसु बार्हताः प्रगाथा आप्यन्त इत्यभीवर्त्तस्तोत्रीया ब्रह्मसामभूतस्य तस्य हि प्रकरणे श्रूयन्ते
10.6.m: [The Brāhmaṇa says:] "In five months the bārhata pragāthas are exhausted"; thus the strophic verses of the Abhīvarta, which serves as the brahma-sāman, are taught in its section.

10.6.s: anyonyaḥ pragātha iti ca nānāpragāthatāṃ darśayati
10.6.d: अन्योन्यः प्रगाथ इति च नानाप्रगाथतां दर्शयति
10.6.m: And the statement, "Each [day has] a different pragātha," indicates the variety of pragāthas.
There are one hundred and four bārhata pragāthas addressed to Indra in the ten maṇḍalas.
Among them, the strophic verses of the Bṛhat, Rathantara, and Kāleya, and the Indrakratu [pragātha], have their places elsewhere.
Of the hundred, one should perform one on the twenty-fourth [day], and the rest in the abhiplavas.

10.6.s: teṣāmekaikaṃ tṛtīye tṛtīye'hani kuryyātkṛtā hyetasmiṃsthāna ārṣeyakalpena
10.6.d: तेषामेकैकं तृतीये तृतीयेऽहनि कुर्य्यात्कृता ह्येतस्मिंस्थान आर्षेयकल्पेन
10.6.m: One should perform one of them on each third day, for they have been assigned to this place by the Ārṣeyakalpa.
In the last abhiplava of the fifth month, on the fifth day, one should use satobṛhatī verses, due to the lack of [bārhata] pragāthas.

10.6.s: teṣvāpteṣu chandasī saṃyujyaitavyamiti ṣaṣṭhe māsi gāyatrīpādamekaikamuṣṇihāmupariṣṭāt kuryādviṣṭāvānupapattirhyanyathā
10.6.d: तेष्वाप्तेषु छन्दसी संयुज्यैतव्यमिति षष्ठे मासि गायत्रीपादमेकैकमुष्णिहामुपरिष्टात् कुर्याद्विष्टावानुपपत्तिर्ह्यन्यथा
10.6.m: [The Brāhmaṇa says:] "When these are exhausted, one must proceed having combined meters"; thus in the sixth month, one should place a gāyatrī quarter-verse after each uṣṇih [verse], for otherwise strophic shifts would not be possible.

10.6.s: sātobārhataśeṣo'ṣṭau tān kṛtvā saṃyoga iti gautamaḥ
10.6.d: सातोबार्हतशेषोऽष्टौ तान् कृत्वा संयोग इति गौतमः
10.6.m: "There is a remainder of eight sātobārhata [triplets]; having performed them, there is the combination [of meters]," says Gautama,
"for they hand down [this rule] because of the exhaustion of the bṛhatī verses."

10.6.s: caturuttaraireva chandobhiretavyamiti gāyatrīṃ caturviśe kuryāduṣṇihaṃ prathama ābhiplavike'nuṣṭubhaṃ dvitīye bṛhatīritareṣu
10.6.d: चतुरुत्तरैरेव छन्दोभिरेतव्यमिति गायत्रीं चतुर्विशे कुर्यादुष्णिहं प्रथम आभिप्लविकेऽनुष्टुभं द्वितीये बृहतीरितरेषु
10.6.m: [The Brāhmaṇa says:] "One must proceed only with meters that increase by four syllables"; thus one should use gāyatrī on the twenty-fourth [day], uṣṇih on the first day of the abhiplava, anuṣṭubh on the second, and bṛhatī verses on the others.

10.6.s: uddharettu pañcamādahnaḥ satobṛhatīḥ prabhavanti hi pragāthāḥ
10.6.d: उद्धरेत्तु पञ्चमादह्नः सतोबृहतीः प्रभवन्ति हि प्रगाथाः
10.6.m: From the fifth day, however, one should remove the satobṛhatī verses, for pragāthas are [now] available.
Having made paṅkti verses there, or in the sixth [month],
they should proceed through the sixth month with triṣṭubh.
The jagatī, however, is [used] on the third svarasāman day.

10.6.s: nava sātobārhataśeṣo dvau ca pragāthau tān kṛtvā paṅktimupeyusteṣāñcottamasyasthāne tata ūrddhvaṃ triṣṭubheti gautamaḥ
10.6.d: नव सातोबार्हतशेषो द्वौ च प्रगाथौ तान् कृत्वा पङ्क्तिमुपेयुस्तेषाञ्चोत्तमस्यस्थाने तत ऊर्द्ध्वं त्रिष्टुभेति गौतमः
10.6.m: "Having performed the remainder of nine sātobārhata [triplets] and two pragāthas, they should adopt the paṅkti, and in place of the last of them, from then onward with triṣṭubh," says Gautama.

10.7.s: bṛhatyā caiva triṣṭubhā caitavyamiti triṣṭubhaṃ caturviṃśe kuryādbṛhatīṃ prathama ābhiplavike
10.7.d: बृहत्या चैव त्रिष्टुभा चैतव्यमिति त्रिष्टुभं चतुर्विंशे कुर्याद्बृहतीं प्रथम आभिप्लविके
10.7.m: [The Brāhmaṇa says:] "One must proceed with bṛhatī and triṣṭubh"; thus one should use triṣṭubh on the twenty-fourth [day], and bṛhatī on the first day of the abhiplava.
This inversion applies throughout the entire course.

10.7.s: caturuttaraprayogo bṛhatītriṣṭubhośca viparyāsaḥ ṣaṣṭha eva māsi syāditi śaucivṛkṣiḥ sśara iva vā eṣa chandasāmiti hi tasminnupodya vidadhāti
10.7.d: चतुरुत्तरप्रयोगो बृहतीत्रिष्टुभोश्च विपर्यासः षष्ठ एव मासि स्यादिति शौचिवृक्षिः स्शर इव वा एष छन्दसामिति हि तस्मिन्नुपोद्य विदधाति
10.7.m: "The employment [of meters] increasing by four syllables and the inversion of bṛhatī and triṣṭubh should occur only in the sixth month," says Śaucivṛkṣi, "for having introduced that [month], [the Brāhmaṇa] prescribes: 'This is, as it were, the head of the meters.'"

10.7.s: sarvatraivetyācāryyāścaturuttarāṇi hyanupūrvaṃ prayuñjāno bṛhatīṃ madhya āmanati triṣṭubhā ṣaṣṭhaṃ māsamiti cāha
10.7.d: सर्वत्रैवेत्याचार्य्याश्चतुरुत्तराणि ह्यनुपूर्वं प्रयुञ्जानो बृहतीं मध्य आमनति त्रिष्टुभा षष्ठं मासमिति चाह
10.7.m: "It applies everywhere," say the teachers, "for employing the meters that increase by four syllables in succession, [the text] mentions bṛhatī in the middle, and says: 'With triṣṭubh [one proceeds through] the sixth month.'"
And because of the exhaustion of bṛhatī verses, an inversion with bṛhatī is not possible.

10.7.s: sā prāyyādbṛhatīgrahaṇamiti śaucivṛkṣistriṣṭubheti yathā bhūyaso vādo'kṣīṇāśca bṛhatyaḥ
10.7.d: सा प्राय्याद्बृहतीग्रहणमिति शौचिवृक्षिस्त्रिष्टुभेति यथा भूयसो वादोऽक्षीणाश्च बृहत्यः
10.7.m: "The mention of bṛhatī is because of its predominance," says Śaucivṛkṣi, "just as the designation 'with triṣṭubh' is [predominant] due to the majority; and the bṛhatī verses are not exhausted,
for there is a remainder of eight sātobārhata [triplets], and the strophic verses of the Bṛhat, Rathantara, and Kāleya; with these one should invert the triṣṭubhs."
[The verse] 'taraṇir it siṣāsati' should be [the base for] the kāleya [melody], since on its day the two strophic verses are [set to] the abhīvarta [sāman].

10.7.s: svarasāmnorvānyatarasmin rathantarastotrīyaṃ kuryāt kṛtā hi tatrānyā rathantarasyaivaṃ vyācakṣata ācāryāḥ
10.7.d: स्वरसाम्नोर्वान्यतरस्मिन् रथन्तरस्तोत्रीयं कुर्यात् कृता हि तत्रान्या रथन्तरस्यैवं व्याचक्षत आचार्याः
10.7.m: Or on either of the two svarasāman [days] one should perform the rathantara strophic verse; for the other [verses] of the rathantara have already been performed there; so explain the teachers.

10.7.s: viṃśatiśataṃ tvapi pragāthā na dhīyate tebhya eva prayuñjīta srodho hi catuḥśate
10.7.d: विंशतिशतं त्वपि प्रगाथा न धीयते तेभ्य एव प्रयुञ्जीत स्रोधो हि चतुःशते
10.7.m: Even if the one hundred and twenty pragāthas are not recited, one should employ [verses] from just those; for in the four hundred [system] there is a continuous flow.
There, in that very manner, one should form satobṛhatī verses.
But one should remove [them] from the fifth day.

10.7.s: śaucivṛkṣeḥ punarviparyāso'nyāyenākṛtakriyā hi vidhānaṃ kṛtāḥ punarbṛhadrathantarakāleyastotrīyāḥ
10.7.d: शौचिवृक्षेः पुनर्विपर्यासोऽन्यायेनाकृतक्रिया हि विधानं कृताः पुनर्बृहद्रथन्तरकालेयस्तोत्रीयाः
10.7.m: Śaucivṛkṣi's inversion, however, is contrary to rule; for an injunction applies to what has not yet been done, whereas the strophic verses for the bṛhat, rathantara, and kāleya have already been made.

10.8.s: vśitiśatasya tu śeṣo vidyate teṣā saptabhiḥ sātobārhataiścaturbhirvyatyasyet
10.8.d: व्शितिशतस्य तु शेषो विद्यते तेषा सप्तभिः सातोबार्हतैश्चतुर्भिर्व्यत्यस्येत्
10.8.m: A remainder of the one hundred and twenty [verses] exists; one should alternate them with seven sātobārhata [verses] and with four.

10.8.s: trayastrśitprabhṛtīn saha caturviśeṣu kuryāduttame ca svarasāmnītyācāryā abhīvartaprakaraṇe hi śrūyante so'trāpyabhīvarta iti
10.8.d: त्रयस्त्र्शित्प्रभृतीन् सह चतुर्विशेषु कुर्यादुत्तमे च स्वरसाम्नीत्याचार्या अभीवर्तप्रकरणे हि श्रूयन्ते सोऽत्राप्यभीवर्त इति
10.8.m: One should perform the thirty-three-stoma days and following together on the caturviṃśa [days] and on the last svarasāman [day], say the teachers, because in the context of the abhīvarta it is heard: 'That is the abhīvarta here too.'

10.8.s: antareṇa tvetāvārṣeyakalpena kṛtṣaṭ pragāthamihāpi tathaiva syāt
10.8.d: अन्तरेण त्वेतावार्षेयकल्पेन कृत्षट् प्रगाथमिहापि तथैव स्यात्
10.8.m: Between these two, however, a group of six pragāthas has been established by the Ārṣeyakalpa; here too it should be just so.

10.8.s: teṣāṃ yatra samaprayoge tṛtīye tṛtīye'hani satobṛhatya upapadyeran kuryādenāstatra
10.8.d: तेषां यत्र समप्रयोगे तृतीये तृतीयेऽहनि सतोबृहत्य उपपद्येरन् कुर्यादेनास्तत्र
10.8.m: Among them, wherever in equal application satobṛhatī verses may be obtained on every third day, one should perform them there.

10.8.s: anupapadyamānāsu pragāthā eva syuranācāro hi ṣaḍahe'nyatra tṛtīyādahnaḥ satobṛhatīnām
10.8.d: अनुपपद्यमानासु प्रगाथा एव स्युरनाचारो हि षडहेऽन्यत्र तृतीयादह्नः सतोबृहतीनाम्
10.8.m: If they are not obtainable, there should be pragāthas alone; for in the six-day period satobṛhatī verses are not customary anywhere other than the third day.

10.8.s: sa yathaiva purastādabhīvarttastotrīyaṃ kuryyāt tathopariṣṭādindrakratau brahmasāmāni nidhanavantyevhyārṣeyakalpena kṛtam
10.8.d: स यथैव पुरस्तादभीवर्त्तस्तोत्रीयं कुर्य्यात् तथोपरिष्टादिन्द्रक्रतौ ब्रह्मसामानि निधनवन्त्येव्ह्यार्षेयकल्पेन कृतम्
10.8.m: Just as he would perform the abhīvarta strophic verse at the beginning, so later in the Indrakratu [stotra] the brahma-sāmans must indeed possess cadences; for so it has been established by the Ārṣeyakalpa.

10.8.s: atirātracaturviśābhyāsaha ṣaṣṭho māsaḥ pūrvasminpakṣasi vratātirātrābhyāṃ prathama uttarasmin
10.8.d: अतिरात्रचतुर्विशाभ्यासह षष्ठो मासः पूर्वस्मिन्पक्षसि व्रतातिरात्राभ्यां प्रथम उत्तरस्मिन्
10.8.m: Together with the atirātra and caturviṃśa [days], the sixth month is in the first half [of the year]; together with the mahāvrata and atirātra, the first [month] is in the second half.

10.8.s: yadetāni sāmāni na cyavanta iti gaurīvitasyottarayornihavaśyāvāśve syātā sarvatra gavāmayane'nārabhya hyacyavanaṃ vidadhātītyeke
10.8.d: यदेतानि सामानि न च्यवन्त इति गौरीवितस्योत्तरयोर्निहवश्यावाश्वे स्याता सर्वत्र गवामयनेऽनारभ्य ह्यच्यवनं विदधातीत्येके
10.8.m: Because of [the rule] 'these sāmans do not fall away', the nihava and the śyāvāśva should be on the two subsequent [verses] of the gaurīvita; everywhere in the Gavāmayana, since it enjoins non-falling-away without specific reference, say some.

10.8.s: anvavetya vidhistvārṣeyakalpena kṛto gaurīvitaśyāvāśvayornihavasya ca brāhmaṇena tathā satyacyavansyāt
10.8.d: अन्ववेत्य विधिस्त्वार्षेयकल्पेन कृतो गौरीवितश्यावाश्वयोर्निहवस्य च ब्राह्मणेन तथा सत्यच्यवन्स्यात्
10.8.m: However, the rule has been established by the Ārṣeyakalpa following [the order of] the gaurīvita and śyāvāśva, and of the nihava by the Brāhmaṇa; when that is so, non-falling-away would be [achieved].

10.9.s: sarve sahartvijo mahāvratena stuvīrannityudgātṛvikāra eva syādaśrutibhūtā hyanye
10.9.d: सर्वे सहर्त्विजो महाव्रतेन स्तुवीरन्नित्युद्गातृविकार एव स्यादश्रुतिभूता ह्यन्ये
10.9.m: Regarding [the text] 'All priests should chant together with the Mahāvrata', this must be an alteration [affecting] the udgātṛ priests alone, for the others have not become the subject of revelation [for chanting].
And the word 'all' is fully applicable to them alone.
Regarding 'they should chant together', because of the combination of ritual actions and the injunction of sequence, the chanting should be in successive order.
And by [the text] 'having chanted as udgītha for himself with three verses', it shows the final chanting by himself.

10.9.s: nānādeśastavanaṃ chandogānāmeva syādudgātaiva sarveṇodgāyediti hyuktvā tasya deśān vidadhāti havirddhāne śirasā stutvā srabdhāḥ pratyañca eyuste dakṣiṇena dhiṣṇyān parītya paścānmaitrāvaruṇasya dhiṣṇyasyopaviśyeti ca ye śirasā stuvate teṣāmevetaraiḥ stavanaṃ darśayati
10.9.d: नानादेशस्तवनं छन्दोगानामेव स्यादुद्गातैव सर्वेणोद्गायेदिति ह्युक्त्वा तस्य देशान् विदधाति हविर्द्धाने शिरसा स्तुत्वा स्रब्धाः प्रत्यञ्च एयुस्ते दक्षिणेन धिष्ण्यान् परीत्य पश्चान्मैत्रावरुणस्य धिष्ण्यस्योपविश्येति च ये शिरसा स्तुवते तेषामेवेतरैः स्तवनं दर्शयति
10.9.m: Chanting in different places must belong only to the Chandogas; for having said 'the udgātṛ alone should chant the udgītha with everything', it enjoins places for him: 'having chanted with the head in the havirdhāna shed, holding onto one another they should go westward, and having gone around the dhiṣṇya hearths to the south, sitting behind the dhiṣṇya hearth of the Maitrāvaruṇa', and it thus indicates chanting by the other [priests] along with those who chant with the head.

10.9.s: ilāndamagniṣṭomasāma kāryyamityagne tava śravo vaya ityetāsāṃ pūrvāsu tisṛṣu syāt
10.9.d: इलान्दमग्निष्टोमसाम कार्य्यमित्यग्ने तव श्रवो वय इत्येतासां पूर्वासु तिसृषु स्यात्
10.9.m: When the ilānda is to be made the agniṣṭoma-sāman, it should be on the first three of these [verses]: 'agne tava śravo vayaḥ'.
The verse-chantings occur on the ten syllables; thus it is in a triplet, just like other sāmans.
On the whole six-verse hymn, say the teachers; the verse-chantings are on the half-verses; thus there is a smoother flow of the songs.

10.9.s: dvādaśarca iti śāṇḍilyastatrāparāvāgneyau tṛcāvāharedā te agne'gniṃ taṃ manya ityevamṛkṣvanugānāni
10.9.d: द्वादशर्च इति शाण्डिल्यस्तत्रापरावाग्नेयौ तृचावाहरेदा ते अग्नेऽग्निं तं मन्य इत्येवमृक्ष्वनुगानानि
10.9.m: On a twelve-verse hymn, says Śāṇḍilya; there one should bring in two other Agni-triplets: 'ā te agne' and 'agniṃ taṃ manye'; thus the verse-chantings are on the verses.

10.9.s: caturthamevānugānaṃ tṛce syāditi vārṣagaṇyo'tra hi nidhanavādaṃ vadati vratamiti bhavati svariti bhavati śakuna iti bhavatīti bhaktayaśca kalpyante nānāsāmavaccainānyeke'dhīyate'dhīyate
10.9.d: चतुर्थमेवानुगानं तृचे स्यादिति वार्षगण्योऽत्र हि निधनवादं वदति व्रतमिति भवति स्वरिति भवति शकुन इति भवतीति भक्तयश्च कल्प्यन्ते नानासामवच्चैनान्येकेऽधीयतेऽधीयते
10.9.m: Only a fourth verse-chanting should be in the triplet, says Vārṣagaṇya; for here it states a teaching on cadences: 'it becomes vratam, it becomes svar, it becomes śakuna', and divisions are arranged; and some study these like distinct sāmans.

10.10.m: For the tenth day of the chandoma ten-day period, the thirty-three-stoma agniṣṭoma-sāman should be the trik-sārparājña, say some, because of the designation of the tenth day.
According to the principle of majority reference, it is the caturviṃśa [day].

10.10.s: ṛksāmāni tu pradiśyante daśamātsarv hyaharadhikṛtya codyate caturviśaḥ
10.10.d: ऋक्सामानि तु प्रदिश्यन्ते दशमात्सर्व् ह्यहरधिकृत्य चोद्यते चतुर्विशः
10.10.m: The ṛk-verses and sāmans, however, are designated from the tenth day; for having taken as governing rule the entire day, the caturviṃśa is enjoined.
And there is direct modification in accordance with the principle of majority reference.

10.10.s: brāhmaṇavihite ca stome kalpapradeśaḥ ṛksāmnāṃ bhavati
10.10.d: ब्राह्मणविहिते च स्तोमे कल्पप्रदेशः ऋक्साम्नां भवति
10.10.m: And when the stoma is enjoined by the Brāhmaṇa, the manual's designation of ṛk-verses and sāmans applies.

10.10.s: triśinaḥ sutyāmāsān sarvatra sañcakṣīran kauṇḍapāyine ca hāviryajñikāstāpaśvite ca daikṣopasadān
10.10.d: त्रिशिनः सुत्यामासान् सर्वत्र सञ्चक्षीरन् कौण्डपायिने च हाविर्यज्ञिकास्तापश्विते च दैक्षोपसदान्
10.10.m: Everywhere they should calculate the soma-pressing months as consisting of thirty days; and in the Kauṇḍapāyina rite the oblation-sacrifice months, and in the Tāpaścita rite the consecration- and upasad-months.
In the course of Dṛti and Vātavant, they should press soma for two deficient months of trivṛt-stomas, says Gautama.
Or both should be of thirty days, according to this Brāhmaṇa.

10.10.s: tathā satyaṣṭamyāṃ dīkṣitvā pañcadaśa dīkṣāḥ kurvīran
10.10.d: तथा सत्यष्टम्यां दीक्षित्वा पञ्चदश दीक्षाः कुर्वीरन्
10.10.m: That being so, having consecrated themselves on the eighth [day], they should perform fifteen consecration days.

10.10.s: pañcadaśānāṃ daśamasyāṣṭādṣṭrāntānyukthāni syurityācāryāḥ ṣoḍaśyapāyāddhi nivṛttaṃ nārmedhamiti
10.10.d: पञ्चदशानां दशमस्याष्टाद्ष्ट्रान्तान्युक्थानि स्युरित्याचार्याः षोडश्यपायाद्धि निवृत्तं नार्मेधमिति
10.10.m: Of the fifteen [days], the uktha lauds of the tenth [day] should end with the aṣṭādaṣṭra sāman, say the teachers; for because of the removal of the ṣoḍaśin, the nārmedha sāman is discontinued.
However, in the absence of a specific statement, discontinuance would not occur, just as in the case of other sāmans.
And the specific statement is the cause [of using] the nārmedha, not the ṣoḍaśin.
And it is frequently seen in rites without the ṣoḍaśin.
Regarding the variations of this session: each month should proceed with the pṛṣṭhya six-day period, say some.
With the abhiplava and pṛṣṭhya [periods], says Śaucivṛkṣi.
With each single day of the pṛṣṭhya period, say Śāṇḍilyāyana and Dhānañjayya.

10.10.s: jyotiṣṭomeneti lāmakāyanastasya rathantaraṃ pṛṣṭhaṃ bṛhacca vyatyāsam
10.10.d: ज्योतिष्टोमेनेति लामकायनस्तस्य रथन्तरं पृष्ठं बृहच्च व्यत्यासम्
10.10.m: With the jyotiṣṭoma, says Lāmakāyana; its pṛṣṭha laud alternating between the rathantara and the bṛhat.

10.11.m: The consecrations of the Kauṇḍapāyina rite begin on the full-moon day.

10.11.s: tasyopasadanta upavasathakarma kṛtvātirātramupeyuriti śāṇḍilya ev hi gṛhyate vṛttiḥ
10.11.d: तस्योपसदन्त उपवसथकर्म कृत्वातिरात्रमुपेयुरिति शाण्डिल्य एव् हि गृह्यते वृत्तिः
10.11.m: At the end of the upasads, having performed the preparation-day rite, they should undertake the atirātra, says Śāṇḍilya; for this practice is traditionally adopted.

10.11.s: tata ūrddhvaṃ prātarāhutyupakramāḥ sāyamāhutissthā ekānnatrśitamahānyagnihotraṃ juhuyuḥ
10.11.d: तत ऊर्द्ध्वं प्रातराहुत्युपक्रमाः सायमाहुतिस्स्था एकान्नत्र्शितमहान्यग्निहोत्रं जुहुयुः
10.11.m: Thereafter, beginning with the morning oblation and ending with the evening oblation, they should offer the agnihotra for twenty-nine days.

10.11.s: māsameveti gautamaḥ sutyānāntu purastādupavasathakarma syādatirātraścaivañca gṛhyate vṛttiravyavāyaśca haviryajñaiḥ sutyānām
10.11.d: मासमेवेति गौतमः सुत्यानान्तु पुरस्तादुपवसथकर्म स्यादतिरात्रश्चैवञ्च गृह्यते वृत्तिरव्यवायश्च हविर्यज्ञैः सुत्यानाम्
10.11.m: For a month exactly, says Gautama; but prior to the soma-pressing days there should be the preparation-day rite and the atirātra; and thus this practice is adopted, and there is no interruption of the soma-pressing days by the oblation sacrifices.

10.11.s: aśravaṇādatirātro na syāditi dhānañjayyaḥ pratyantāddhyanyeṣu codayanneha vidadhāti
10.11.d: अश्रवणादतिरात्रो न स्यादिति धानञ्जय्यः प्रत्यन्ताद्ध्यन्येषु चोदयन्नेह विदधाति
10.11.m: Because it is not mentioned in revelation, there should be no atirātra, says Dhānañjayya; for enjoining it from the border ritual in other cases, it does not prescribe it here.
At the very end of the upasads, the preparation-day rite should take place.

10.11.s: aṣṭādaśabhyo vorddhvśaunāsīryyebhyo rājānaṃ krīṇīyurevamanantar sutyābhyo bhavatīti
10.11.d: अष्टादशभ्यो वोर्द्ध्व्शौनासीर्य्येभ्यो राजानं क्रीणीयुरेवमनन्तर् सुत्याभ्यो भवतीति
10.11.m: Or after the eighteen Śunāsīrīya offerings, they should purchase King Soma; thus it is immediately contiguous to the soma-pressing days.

10.11.s: dīkṣopasadāṃ vyavāyo nyāya iti śāṇḍilyāyanaste māsi somaṃ krīṇantīti vānantaraṃ dīkṣābhyaḥ krayaṃ darśayati
10.11.d: दीक्षोपसदां व्यवायो न्याय इति शाण्डिल्यायनस्ते मासि सोमं क्रीणन्तीति वानन्तरं दीक्षाभ्यः क्रयं दर्शयति
10.11.m: The separation of the consecrations and the upasads is the proper rule, says Śāṇḍilyāyana; or [the text] 'they purchase soma in that month' shows the purchase immediately after the consecrations.
The preparation-day rite alone should be immediately contiguous to the soma-pressing days.

10.11.s: āgnīdhrīyādaṅgārānmārjālīyhṛtvā pṛthak sthālīpākān śrapayitvā pitṛyajñān kurvīran
10.11.d: आग्नीध्रीयादङ्गारान्मार्जालीय्हृत्वा पृथक् स्थालीपाकान् श्रपयित्वा पितृयज्ञान् कुर्वीरन्
10.11.m: Having taken embers from the āgnīdhra hearth to the mārjālīya hearth and having cooked separate mess-offerings of boiled grain, they should perform ancestral sacrifices.
Then, in the ancestral sacrifice, they should carry forward [the fire] southwards.

10.11.s: āhavanīyāddakṣiṇato varuṇapraghāseṣu tasmin kuryyuryaddakṣiṇāhavanīye kṛtyamupavasathakarma cet kṛtsyāt
10.11.d: आहवनीयाद्दक्षिणतो वरुणप्रघासेषु तस्मिन् कुर्य्युर्यद्दक्षिणाहवनीये कृत्यमुपवसथकर्म चेत् कृत्स्यात्
10.11.m: South of the āhavanīya fire in the Varuṇapraghāsa rites they should perform in it whatever duty belongs to the southern āhavanīya fire, if the preparatory rite has been performed completely.
In the month of the agnihotra, the adhvaryu priest should offer the food of the consecrated [sacrificers]; the others should be holding on [to him].
In the course of the iṣṭi offerings, they should cut off portions only from the sacrificial foods.

10.12.s: agnihotropasthānaṃ viṣṇukramāḥ samiṣṭayajūṣīti na kriyerannavabhṛthanyaṅgaśceti śāṇḍilyaḥ
10.12.d: अग्निहोत्रोपस्थानं विष्णुक्रमाः समिष्टयजूषीति न क्रियेरन्नवभृथन्यङ्गश्चेति शाण्डिल्यः
10.12.m: The attendance on the agnihotra, the steps of Viṣṇu, and the samiṣṭayajus formulas should not be performed, nor the minor rites of the avabhṛtha, says Śāṇḍilya.
However, they should place the kindling sticks that have been mentioned earlier there.
Everything should be performed, says Dhānañjayya.
Regarding [the rule]: 'For a month with the new- and full-moon sacrifices'—[they should perform] the first fortnight with the new-moon sacrifice, and the other with the full-moon sacrifice.

10.12.s: āmāvāsye pitṛyajñaḥ sakṛdbhūtvā na syāditi gautamaḥ
10.12.d: आमावास्ये पितृयज्ञः सकृद्भूत्वा न स्यादिति गौतमः
10.12.m: At the new-moon sacrifice, the rite for the ancestors having occurred once should not take place again, says Gautama.
It should not take place even once, says Śāṇḍilya.
It should take place day after day, says Dhānañjayya.

10.12.s: māssākamedhairiti gṛhamedhīyeneṣṭvā tadaiva śeṣssthāpayeyurevaṃ trśitkṛtva upetā bhavantīti
10.12.d: मास्साकमेधैरिति गृहमेधीयेनेष्ट्वा तदैव शेष्स्स्थापयेयुरेवं त्र्शित्कृत्व उपेता भवन्तीति
10.12.m: Regarding [the rule]: 'For a month with the Sākamedha rites'—having sacrificed with the Gṛhamedhīya rite, they should establish the remainder on that very day; 'in this manner they have undertaken it thirty times,' [says the text].

10.12.s: dvyahāpavargastveṣāṃ prakṛtau pañcadaśakṛtva evābhyasyeyuḥ sa māsaḥ
10.12.d: द्व्यहापवर्गस्त्वेषां प्रकृतौ पञ्चदशकृत्व एवाभ्यस्येयुः स मासः
10.12.m: Their completion in the archetype takes two days; they should repeat it fifteen times: that is a month.
Regarding [the text]: 'The agnihotra is the Daśahotṛ'—the adhvaryus recite the attendance on the agnihotra called Daśahotṛ.
The officiating priests are intended by the subsequent [formulas].
They should consume [the soma] with handleless cups shaped like bowls.
The combination [of duties] with the hotṛ priest has been stated by the Brāhmaṇa.
The brahman priest should move up from his own seat to the other, the hotṛ priest.
Likewise the udgātṛ priest and the prastotṛ priest, and the āgnīdhra priest.
'The householder is the householder; the subrahmaṇya priest is the subrahmaṇya priest': thus [the text] shows that there is no combination for the two.

10.13.m: By this, the consecration and following rites of the Tāpaścita sacrifice are explained.
The Jyotiṣṭoma atirātra sacrifice equipped with the ṣoḍaśin should take place day after day, says Dhānañjayya.

10.13.s: catvāro jyotiṣṭomā abhijideṣa pañcāhaḥ ṣaṭsu māseṣvabhyasyeta mahāvrataṃ viṣuvānathaita eva māsā āvṛttā viśvajittvabhijitsthāne tatpuruṣasya nārāyaṇasyāyanam
10.13.d: चत्वारो ज्योतिष्टोमा अभिजिदेष पञ्चाहः षट्सु मासेष्वभ्यस्येत महाव्रतं विषुवानथैत एव मासा आवृत्ता विश्वजित्त्वभिजित्स्थाने तत्पुरुषस्य नारायणस्यायनम्
10.13.m: Four Jyotiṣṭomas and the Abhijit: this five-day rite should be repeated over six months; the Mahāvrata is the Viṣuvant day; then these very months are repeated, but the Viśvajit replaces the Abhijit: that is the course of Puruṣa Nārāyaṇa.
The Abhijit [takes place] day after day; that belongs to Agni, or it is a Jyotiṣṭoma with the rathantara pṛṣṭha laud.
Alternating the bṛhat and rathantara as the pṛṣṭha laud, that belongs to Indrāgnī.
The one having both sāmans belongs to Brahman and Prajāpati.
The one with the vairūpa pṛṣṭha laud, or the vrata day, belongs to Vāyu.
The one with the vairāja pṛṣṭha laud, or the Viśvajit, belongs to Āditya.
The one with the vāmadevya pṛṣṭha laud belongs to Prajāpati.
The one with the svar pṛṣṭha laud belongs to the All-gods.
The one with the divākīrtya pṛṣṭha laud belongs to Sūrya.
The one with the mahāvrata pṛṣṭha laud belongs to Mahendra.

10.13.s: jyotiṣṭomena trīṇyuttarāṇi tasya rathantaraṃ pṛṣṭhaṃ bṛhacca vyatyāsam
10.13.d: ज्योतिष्टोमेन त्रीण्युत्तराणि तस्य रथन्तरं पृष्ठं बृहच्च व्यत्यासम्
10.13.m: Three subsequent [rites] are performed with the Jyotiṣṭoma; its pṛṣṭha laud is the rathantara and the bṛhat alternately.

10.14.s: agniṣṭomāstrivṛta ukthyāḥ para iti tatrāvacanādatirātrā na syurviṣuvantaśceti śāṇḍilyaḥ
10.14.d: अग्निष्टोमास्त्रिवृत उक्थ्याः पर इति तत्रावचनादतिरात्रा न स्युर्विषुवन्तश्चेति शाण्डिल्यः
10.14.m: Regarding [the text]: 'The trivṛt agniṣṭoma sacrifices are followed by the ukthya sacrifices'—because there is no statement there, there should be no atirātra sacrifices nor Viṣuvant days, says Śāṇḍilya.
The other rule of the sattra applies, says Dhānañjayya.

10.14.s: atirātrāvabhitaḥ syātāṃ madhye viṣuvān bṛhatpṛṣṭho rathantaramadhyandinaḥ pañcadaśaḥ saptadaśaḥ
10.14.d: अतिरात्रावभितः स्यातां मध्ये विषुवान् बृहत्पृष्ठो रथन्तरमध्यन्दिनः पञ्चदशः सप्तदशः
10.14.m: Two atirātra sacrifices should be on both sides; in the middle is the Viṣuvant day, having the bṛhat pṛṣṭha laud, the rathantara at the midday pressing, and a fifteenfold and seventeenfold [stoma].
Or this should take place in each single group of years.
Or the highest [rite] should take place in the highest year.
Their Viṣuvant days should correspond to their stomas.

With the trivṛt stoma, it should have the rathantara pṛṣṭha laud and the bṛhat as the brahman's sāman; in the subsequent ones, it should have the bṛhat pṛṣṭha laud and the rathantara at the midday pressing.

10.14.s: yajanīye'hani prasavaḥ syāt pūrvvapakṣe yadyaviṣuvatkāḥ samārddhamāsātivarttiṣu
10.14.d: यजनीयेऽहनि प्रसवः स्यात् पूर्व्वपक्षे यद्यविषुवत्काः समार्द्धमासातिवर्त्तिषु
10.14.m: The pressing should take place on the sacrificial day in the first fortnight, if [the rites] are without Viṣuvant days in those that pass over an even half-month.
In the thousand-pressing rite, there are a thousand days together with the two atirātras, say the teachers; for it says: 'a thousand-pressing rite.'
Between [the two], says Śaucivṛkṣi, for [the text] says: 'a thousand days between the two atirātras.'
The option for its course is: the trikadruka rites, one hundred and sixty-four abhiplava periods, the ten-day period, and the vrata day; the ten-day period, and the vrata day.

10.15.s: dakṣiṇe tīre sarasvatyā vinaśanasya dīkṣeran sārasvatāya ṣaṣṭhyāmpakṣasyeti gautamaḥ
10.15.d: दक्षिणे तीरे सरस्वत्या विनशनस्य दीक्षेरन् सारस्वताय षष्ठ्याम्पक्षस्येति गौतमः
10.15.m: They should consecrate themselves on the southern bank of the Sarasvatī at Vinaśana for the Sarasvatī session on the sixth day of the fortnight, says Gautama.
The atirātra sacrifice should be on the new moon day; thus the rite belonging to the new moon is applied in its proper place.

10.15.s: saptamyāṃ vā dīkṣitvāmāvāsyāyā yajanīye'hanyatirātraḥ syāditi dhānañjayyaḥ
10.15.d: सप्तम्यां वा दीक्षित्वामावास्याया यजनीयेऽहन्यतिरात्रः स्यादिति धानञ्जय्यः
10.15.m: Or having consecrated themselves on the seventh day, the atirātra sacrifice should be on the sacrificial day of the new moon, says Dhānañjayya.
The resolutions [are effected] by the two subsequent soma-pressing days.
And the new-moon sacrifice is performed in its proper place.
For the first half of the month is the place of the new-moon sacrifice.

10.15.s: purā rātreḥ sāyaṃ dohaṃ dohayeran ssthite'tirātre prātardohaṃ tena sānnāyyena yajeran
10.15.d: पुरा रात्रेः सायं दोहं दोहयेरन् स्स्थितेऽतिरात्रे प्रातर्दोहं तेन सान्नाय्येन यजेरन्
10.15.m: Before nightfall they should have the evening milking done; when the atirātra sacrifice has concluded, the morning milking; with that curd-and-milk mixture they should sacrifice.

10.15.s: sānnāyyeneṣṭvādhvaryuḥ śamyāṃ parāsyatītyāhavanīyanyantena tiṣṭhan prāṅmukho nityamiṣṭissthāsu prāsyettaduktaṃ brāhmaṇena
10.15.d: सान्नाय्येनेष्ट्वाध्वर्युः शम्यां परास्यतीत्याहवनीयन्यन्तेन तिष्ठन् प्राङ्मुखो नित्यमिष्टिस्स्थासु प्रास्येत्तदुक्तं ब्राह्मणेन
10.15.m: Standing facing east along the border of the āhavanīya fire, [the adhvaryu priest] should regularly cast the wooden peg at the conclusions of the sacrifices, in accordance with the text: 'Having sacrificed with the curd-and-milk mixture, the adhvaryu priest throws the wooden peg away'; that is stated by the Brāhmaṇa.
And thus also the hall for the wife and the slaughter-place should have wheels.
They should roll them each to its place, if the plot of ground is level.
They should take dust from the altar, likewise from the high altar and from the hearth-mounds.
Having settled, they should scatter them according to their proper places.
Regarding 'the sacrificial post has a mortar-shaped base,' it should have a broad base.
Regarding 'having dragged [it],' they should simply drag it forward without lifting it up.
Regarding 'just heaped about,' it should stand unburied, banked around with dust.

10.15.s: noparavān khanantītyadhiṣavaṇaphalakayoradhastāduparavā nāma śvabhrāsteṣāṃ pratiṣedha ālikheyurevainānna khaneyuḥ
10.15.d: नोपरवान् खनन्तीत्यधिषवणफलकयोरधस्तादुपरवा नाम श्वभ्रास्तेषां प्रतिषेध आलिखेयुरेवैनान्न खनेयुः
10.15.m: Regarding 'they do not dig the sounding-holes,' the sounding-holes are holes beneath the two pressing-boards; there is a prohibition of them: they should merely outline them and not dig them.

10.16.s: teṣāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ goṣṭomaḥ stomo bhavatīti yajanīye'hani syādityācāryāḥ ssthite goṣṭome paurṇamāsamiti hi ssthānāntādvidadhāti
10.16.d: तेषां पौर्णमास्यां गोष्टोमः स्तोमो भवतीति यजनीयेऽहनि स्यादित्याचार्याः स्स्थिते गोष्टोमे पौर्णमासमिति हि स्स्थानान्ताद्विदधाति
10.16.m: Regarding 'for them the goṣṭoma becomes the stoma on the full-moon day,' the teachers say it should be on the day fit for sacrifice; for [the Brāhmaṇa] enjoins the full-moon sacrifice from the end of the completion, once the goṣṭoma has concluded.
And the mention of the fortnights in 'they [spend] it waxing, they [spend] it waning' applies to them as wholes.

10.16.s: parvaṇi tveva syātteṣāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ teṣāmamāvāsyāyāmiti hi pratyakṣeṇa vidadhāti
10.16.d: पर्वणि त्वेव स्यात्तेषां पौर्णमास्यां तेषाममावास्यायामिति हि प्रत्यक्षेण विदधाति
10.16.m: However, it should indeed occur on the change of the moon; for it enjoins directly: 'for them on the full moon, for them on the new moon.'
The completion is merely immediate sequence of ritual actions for the new- and full-moon sacrifices.

10.16.s: te tamāpūryamāṇante tamapakṣīyamāṇamiti ca yathā bhūyaso vādaḥ
10.16.d: ते तमापूर्यमाणन्ते तमपक्षीयमाणमिति च यथा भूयसो वादः
10.16.m: And the statement 'they [spend] it waxing, they [spend] it waning' is according to the predominant part.
When the goṣṭoma has concluded, having sacrificed that very day with the full-moon sacrificial oblation, they should prepare to depart.
Without sacrificing, they should spend that night in that very place, says Gautama.
They should certainly prepare to depart, says Śāṇḍilya, but on the morrow they should sacrifice.
There, according to Dhānañjayya, they should have the evening milking done for the new moon, [and] the morning milking before the morning litany.
The curd-and-milk mixture thus milked would sit for too long, says Śāṇḍilyāyana; they should do one or the other of the two alternative [practices].
In the Kauṇḍapāyina sacrificial session, the feeding and the rules of the new- and full-moon sacrifices have been stated for the sacrifice-courses.

10.16.s: candrapramāṇāstveva parvasu s ya u ḥ
10.16.m: However, at the changes of the moon they should be measured by the moon.

10.17.m: At the confluence of the Dṛṣadvatī, they should offer the oblation to Apāṁ Napāt if it contains water.
Even if it is without water, says Dhānañjayya.
Regarding 'they introduce a bull among a hundred cows,' [this means] among a hundred pregnant young heifers.
Where there is bovine safety, there they should protect them.
They should support themselves by means of their bullocks and with clarified butter.

10.17.s: tāsu sahasrsampannāsu pūrvapakṣe gāmatirātraṃ kṛtvā dattvaitā uttiṣṭheyuḥ
10.17.d: तासु सहस्र्सम्पन्नासु पूर्वपक्षे गामतिरात्रं कृत्वा दत्त्वैता उत्तिष्ठेयुः
10.17.m: When they have multiplied to a thousand, having performed the cow-atirātra sacrifice in the first half of the month and having given these away, they should conclude the session.

10.17.s: yadā sarvajyāniñjīyanta iti tāsāmevādhikāraḥ prakaraṇabhūtatvāttatra viśvajidatirātraḥ
10.17.d: यदा सर्वज्यानिञ्जीयन्त इति तासामेवाधिकारः प्रकरणभूतत्वात्तत्र विश्वजिदतिरात्रः
10.17.m: Regarding 'when they suffer total ruin,' the rule applies only to these [cattle] because of the context; in that case the viśvajit-atirātra sacrifice [is performed].
Upon the emergence of either of these two misfortunes, they should conclude the session, even in the second half of the month.
They should not descend into the Sarasvatī for the concluding purificatory bath even once, for it serves as their sacrificial ground.
If none is found, [they may take] an extraction from the Sarasvatī, but off to the side.

10.17.s: yadā plakṣaṃ prāsravaṇamāgacchantyathotthānamiti tathā prāsyeyuryathainaṃ pūrvapakṣa āgaccheyuriti gautamaḥ
10.17.d: यदा प्लक्षं प्रास्रवणमागच्छन्त्यथोत्थानमिति तथा प्रास्येयुर्यथैनं पूर्वपक्ष आगच्छेयुरिति गौतमः
10.17.m: Regarding 'when they come to Plakṣa Prāsravaṇa, then is the conclusion,' they should throw [the peg] in such a way that they arrive there in the first half of the month, says Gautama.
Whenever they reach this, the conclusion should take place, says Dhānañjayya; undertaking just the opening atirātra sacrifice, they should conclude the session.

10.17.s: plakṣaṃ prāsravaṇamāgamya purastādatirātrasyāgnaye kāmāyeṣṭiḥ syāditi śāṇḍilyaḥ
10.17.d: प्लक्षं प्रास्रवणमागम्य पुरस्तादतिरात्रस्याग्नये कामायेष्टिः स्यादिति शाण्डिल्यः
10.17.m: Having reached Plakṣa Prāsravaṇa, the oblation to Agni Kāma should take place prior to the atirātra sacrifice, says Śāṇḍilya.
At that [oblation], they should give a mare, a slave woman, two milch-cows, and the remaining sacrificial utensils to another worthy person.

10.17.s: svāmino hi sarve satreṣu teṣāṃ pratigrahaṃ na vidyate
10.17.d: स्वामिनो हि सर्वे सत्रेषु तेषां प्रतिग्रहं न विद्यते
10.17.m: For all are masters in sacrificial sessions; acceptance of gifts is not found among them.
The concluding purificatory bath has been stated by the Brāhmaṇa.

10.18.m: By this itself the subsequent two [sacrifices] are explained.
There, the oblation to Agni Kāma and the one to Apāṁ Napāt should be two offerings with the dipping-ladle.
If it is after the atirātra sacrifice, it should be an oblation alone to Agni Kāma, says Śāṇḍilya.

10.18.s: pūrvasyāgniṣṭomau trivṛtī rāthantarabārhate pūrvapakṣa ukthye pañcadaśe rāthantarabārhate aparapakṣa iti gautamaḥ
10.18.d: पूर्वस्याग्निष्टोमौ त्रिवृती राथन्तरबार्हते पूर्वपक्ष उक्थ्ये पञ्चदशे राथन्तरबार्हते अपरपक्ष इति गौतमः
10.18.m: The two agniṣṭoma sacrifices of the former are threefold [stomas] with Rathantara and Bṛhat melodies in the first half of the month; the two ukthya sacrifices are fifteenfold [stomas] with Rathantara and Bṛhat melodies in the second half of the month, says Gautama.
He should not transpose them between the two fortnights.
Everywhere, however, the threefold and fifteenfold [stomas] should be alternating.
With whichever of the two has not been undertaken when the change of the moon arrives, with that he should begin the subsequent fortnight.
By this the rule for the subsequent [session] among the Trikadruka rites has been stated.
The observances for the two [rites] along the Dṛṣadvatī.

10.18.s: tiṣṭheddivāsīta nakt havirucchiṣṭabhojī syādadhaḥsaṃveśyamāsāśyalavaṇāśī na striyamupeyādyathā prakṛtyāhitāgnivṛttiṃ vartayet
10.18.d: तिष्ठेद्दिवासीत नक्त् हविरुच्छिष्टभोजी स्यादधःसंवेश्यमासाश्यलवणाशी न स्त्रियमुपेयाद्यथा प्रकृत्याहिताग्निवृत्तिं वर्तयेत्
10.18.m: He should stand by day, sit by night, eat the remnants of the sacrificial oblation, sleep on the ground, eat flesh and salt, not approach a woman, and conduct the livelihood of an āhitāgni according to the basic model.

10.18.s: dārṣadvate saṃvatsaraṃ brāhmaṇasya gārakṣedityṛtvija ācāryyasya vā
10.18.d: दार्षद्वते संवत्सरं ब्राह्मणस्य गारक्षेदित्यृत्विज आचार्य्यस्य वा
10.18.m: In the rite along the Dṛṣadvatī, regarding 'he should guard the cows of a brāhmaṇa for a year,' [this means] of an officiating priest or of the teacher.

10.18.s: naitandhavānā mārmāḥ sarasvatyāṃ teṣāmeko vyarṇastasmin saṃvatsaramagnimindhīta yaikāgneḥ paricaryyā tayā
10.18.d: नैतन्धवाना मार्माः सरस्वत्यां तेषामेको व्यर्णस्तस्मिन् संवत्सरमग्निमिन्धीत यैकाग्नेः परिचर्य्या तया
10.18.m: Naitandhava is a lake on the Sarasvatī; one [portion] of these is Vyarṇa: there he should kindle the fire for a year according to the service proper to a single fire.
If he was previously an āhitāgni, [he tends it] merely offering the agnihotra.

10.19.s: saṃvatsarādūrddhvaṃ parīṇaṃ nāma sthalī kurukṣetre tasyāmagnīnādhāya yathākālamanvārambhaṇīyayeṣṭvā prasṛjyeteti śāṇḍilyaḥ
10.19.d: संवत्सरादूर्द्ध्वं परीणं नाम स्थली कुरुक्षेत्रे तस्यामग्नीनाधाय यथाकालमन्वारम्भणीययेष्ट्वा प्रसृज्येतेति शाण्डिल्यः
10.19.m: After a year, having established the fires on a raised ground called Parīṇat in Kurukṣetra, and having offered the anvārambhaṇīyā offering at the proper time, he should set forth: so says Śāṇḍilya.
He should sacrifice with the new- and full-moon offerings: so says Dhānañjayya.
If he was previously an āhitāgni, having merely offered the evening and morning oblations [he proceeds].
Having reached the confluence of the Sarasvatī and the Dṛṣadvatī, he should begin sacrificing with [a cake] on eight potsherds for Agni.
There the hurling of the yoke-pin is as in the Sarasvatī rites.
However, he should not stride beyond the standard stride.
At will, he may complete more than one offering in a single day.
He should proceed along the southern bank of the Dṛṣadvatī.

10.19.s: tasyāḥ prabhavyamarmaṃ prāpyaitayeṣṭyeṣṭvā triplakṣāvaharaṇaṃ prati yamunāmavabhṛthamabhyaveyāt
10.19.d: तस्याः प्रभव्यमर्मं प्राप्यैतयेष्ट्येष्ट्वा त्रिप्लक्षावहरणं प्रति यमुनामवभृथमभ्यवेयात्
10.19.m: Having reached Prabhavyamarma [on that river] and having sacrificed with that offering, he should descend into the Yamunā opposite Triplakṣāvaharaṇa for the avabhṛtha.

10.19.s: yatra kvaca tato dūre yamunā syāt tatraitayeṣṭyeṣṭvā svaysāma gāyannavabhṛthamabhyaveyādagāyanvā
10.19.d: यत्र क्वच ततो दूरे यमुना स्यात् तत्रैतयेष्ट्येष्ट्वा स्वय्साम गायन्नवभृथमभ्यवेयादगायन्वा
10.19.m: Wherever far from there the Yamunā may be, having sacrificed there with that offering, he should descend for the avabhṛtha singing the svayansāman, or without singing.
"I consider this to be the journey of one about to renounce the world," says Dhānañjayya, "for thus he disappears from human beings."
As if [saying]: he should not return to the village.
He ascends to the heavenly world.
Or rather, he turns away [from evil] and becomes more excellent.
Or on account of disappearance into the water, as [in the case of] Sarajas.

10.20.m: For a year he should sacrifice day by day with the stauṣa.

10.20.s: ṣaṣṭhyāṃ caitrīpakṣasya pañcamyāmiti gautamo vratopāyanīyamodanamaśitvā keśaśmaśrūṇi vāpayitvāhataṃ vasanaṃ paridhāya parisamuhyāgnīn paristīryya praṇītāḥ praṇīya mekhalāmābadhya daṇḍe pāṇau kṛtvā paścādgārhapatyasyopaviśya svayaṃ kṛṣṇājinaṃ pratiṣajeta tūṣṇīm
10.20.d: षष्ठ्यां चैत्रीपक्षस्य पञ्चम्यामिति गौतमो व्रतोपायनीयमोदनमशित्वा केशश्मश्रूणि वापयित्वाहतं वसनं परिधाय परिसमुह्याग्नीन् परिस्तीर्य्य प्रणीताः प्रणीय मेखलामाबध्य दण्डे पाणौ कृत्वा पश्चाद्गार्हपत्यस्योपविश्य स्वयं कृष्णाजिनं प्रतिषजेत तूष्णीम्

10.20.m: Passing behind the āhavanīya toward the south, he should do this.

10.20.s: tasya tisra iṣṭayaḥ pūrvāhṇa ekā pṛthak ca madhyandināparāhṇayoḥ
10.20.d: तस्य तिस्र इष्टयः पूर्वाह्ण एका पृथक् च मध्यन्दिनापराह्णयोः
10.20.m: His offerings are three: one in the forenoon, and separately at midday and in the afternoon.
In those [offerings he offers] successively the separate sacrificial offerings that are prescribed by the Brāhmaṇa.

10.20.s: ekā vaiva syāttasyāṃ tāni sarvāṇi syuḥ
10.20.d: एका वैव स्यात्तस्यां तानि सर्वाणि स्युः
10.20.m: Or there may be only one [offering daily], in which all of those [oblations] would be included.
After a year, he should descend for the avabhṛtha; there the singing of the sāman is as in the preceding rite.

10.20.s: ubhayostvavabhṛyādudetya yat purastādiṣṭyayanaṃ teneṣṭvā somena yajeta
10.20.d: उभयोस्त्ववभृयादुदेत्य यत् पुरस्तादिष्ट्ययनं तेनेष्ट्वा सोमेन यजेत
10.20.m: However, emerging from the avabhṛtha of both [rites], having sacrificed with the course of offerings that was earlier, he should sacrifice with soma.
Or with as many animal victims dedicated to those deities as there were sacrificial offerings beforehand.
For [the Brāhmaṇa] says: "Ṣaṇḍa and Kuṣaṇḍa are the abhigara and apagara chanters."
However, it is directly prescribed by the Ārṣeyakalpa; there is no inference [needed] in that regard.
The abhigara and apagara chanters should be present only on the penultimate day.
The three-year rite has its pressing day at the full moon.
As for its dīkṣā days, one may do as one wishes.
Some say that he should interchange the first and last years, in order to mount up to the position of the abhiplava and pṛṣṭhya stomas.
In the thousand-year sacrifice, in the thousand-year sacrifice, having its pressing day at the new moon.
